html:
The Battle of Leipzig, also called the Battle of the Nations, was fought from 16 to 19 October 1813 around the city of Leipzig in Saxony, Germany. The armies of Russia, Prussia, Austria and Sweden beat Napoleon. With over 500,000 soldiers, it was the largest battle in Europe before the First World War.

After Napoleon's disaster in Russia in 1812, Prussia changed sides, and Austria and Sweden followed. Napoleon raised a new army, of young recruits, short of horses. The allies agreed to avoid Napoleon himself, beat his marshals, then close in. At Leipzig they came at him from the north, south and east. On the first day he held them. By 18 October he had under 200,000 men against more than 300,000, and his Saxon troops went over to the enemy in mid-battle. He retreated through the city on the 19th. The one bridge was blown up too early, trapping about 30,000 of his men.

French rule in Germany collapsed, and the Confederation of the Rhine broke up. The allies invaded France and took Paris in March 1814. Napoleon gave up his throne and was sent to Elba, and the victors met at the Congress of Vienna.
